title: Tissues
seo_title: Tissues Class 9 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 6)
standard_text: Tissues, organs, organ system, organism. Structure and functions of animal and plant tissues (only four types of tissues in animals; meristematic and permanent tissues in plants).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 9 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 6: meristematic and permanent plant tissues, xylem and phloem, and epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous tissues in animals. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A tissue is a group of similar cells doing one job.
key_sub: Plants: meristem and permanent tissue. Animals: four types.
body_html:
How to think about it

Plants have meristematic tissue, which keeps dividing at root and shoot tips (apical), in the cambium (lateral) and at the base of leaves (intercalary), and permanent tissue. Simple permanent tissues are parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma; complex tissues are xylem (water) and phloem (food).

Animals have four kinds of tissue: epithelial (covering and lining), connective (blood, bone, cartilage, ligament, tendon, areolar and adipose), muscular (striated, smooth and cardiac) and nervous tissue made of neurons.

Example

Which tissue joins muscle to bone?

strong, little flexibility

Answer: a tendon

Example

Which tissue makes a stem thicker?

cambium divides sideways

Answer: lateral meristem

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up ligaments (bone to bone) and tendons (muscle to bone).
  • Saying xylem carries food.
  • Calling sclerenchyma a living tissue.

faq.q: What is the difference between xylem and phloem?
faq.a: Xylem carries water and minerals upwards; phloem carries food made in the leaves to all parts of the plant.

faq.q: What are the three kinds of muscle?
faq.a: Striated (voluntary) muscle in limbs, smooth (involuntary) muscle in organs such as the stomach, and cardiac muscle in the heart.

items.q: What is the role of xylem in a plant?
c: carrying water and minerals up from the roots
carrying food from the leaves to other parts of the plant
increasing the girth (thickness) of the stem or root
carrying water as the tube-like cells of xylem
items.e: Xylem: carrying water and minerals up from the roots.

items.q: What is the role of aerenchyma in a plant?
c: helping aquatic plants float, using large air cavities
protecting the plant as the outer layer of cells, often with a waxy cuticle
protecting older stems; its dead cells have suberin, which keeps out water and gases
items.e: Aerenchyma: helping aquatic plants float, using large air cavities.

items.q: What is the role of companion cells in a plant?
c: protecting the plant as the outer layer of cells, often with a waxy cuticle
protecting older stems; its dead cells have suberin, which keeps out water and gases
carrying water and minerals up from the roots
living cells next to sieve tubes that help them work
items.e: Companion cells: living cells next to sieve tubes that help them work.

items.q: Which plant tissue is mainly found in the stem of a lotus or water hyacinth?
items.e: The stem of a lotus or water hyacinth: aerenchyma.

items.q: What is the role of sclerenchyma in a plant?
c: hardness and strength, with dead cells and lignin in their walls
carrying food from the leaves to other parts of the plant
protecting the plant as the outer layer of cells, often with a waxy cuticle
items.e: Sclerenchyma: hardness and strength, with dead cells and lignin in their walls.

items.q: Which plant tissue is responsible for increasing the length of the stem and the root?
items.e: Apical meristem: increasing the length of the stem and the root.

items.q: What is the role of apical meristem in a plant?
c: living cells next to sieve tubes that help them work
growth at the base of leaves or the internodes
increasing the length of the stem and the root
carrying water and minerals up from the roots
items.e: Apical meristem: increasing the length of the stem and the root.

items.q: What is the role of sieve tubes in a plant?
c: living cells next to sieve tubes that help them work
carrying food from the leaves to other parts of the plant
carrying food as the tube cells of phloem with perforated walls
carrying water as the tube-like cells of xylem
items.e: Sieve tubes: carrying food as the tube cells of phloem with perforated walls.

items.q: Which plant tissue is mainly found in the bark of a tree?
items.e: The bark of a tree: cork.

items.q: Which plant tissue is mainly found in the tubes carrying sugar down from the leaves?
items.e: The tubes carrying sugar down from the leaves: phloem.

items.q: What is the role of tracheids and vessels in a plant?
c: storing food, with thin walls and loosely packed cells
increasing the length of the stem and the root
carrying water as the tube-like cells of xylem
carrying food from the leaves to other parts of the plant
items.e: Tracheids and vessels: carrying water as the tube-like cells of xylem.

items.q: Which plant tissue is mainly found in the hard shell of a walnut?
items.e: The hard shell of a walnut: sclerenchyma.

items.q: What is the role of epidermis in a plant?
c: living cells next to sieve tubes that help them work
protecting the plant as the outer layer of cells, often with a waxy cuticle
hardness and strength, with dead cells and lignin in their walls
increasing the girth (thickness) of the stem or root
items.e: Epidermis: protecting the plant as the outer layer of cells, often with a waxy cuticle.

items.q: Which plant tissue is mainly found in the base of grass leaves?
items.e: The base of grass leaves: intercalary meristem.

items.q: What is the role of phloem in a plant?
c: flexibility in leaves and stems, with cells thickened at the corners
carrying water as the tube-like cells of xylem
carrying food from the leaves to other parts of the plant
items.e: Phloem: carrying food from the leaves to other parts of the plant.

items.q: Which plant tissue is mainly found in the starch-storing cortex of a root?
items.e: The starch-storing cortex of a root: parenchyma.

items.q: Which plant tissue is responsible for flexibility in leaves and stems, with cells thickened at the corners?
items.e: Collenchyma: flexibility in leaves and stems, with cells thickened at the corners.

items.q: Which plant tissue is responsible for protecting older stems; its dead cells have suberin, which keeps out water and gases?
items.e: Cork: protecting older stems; its dead cells have suberin, which keeps out water and gases.

items.q: Which plant tissue is mainly found in the fibres of jute?
items.e: The fibres of jute: sclerenchyma.

items.q: What is the role of guard cells in a plant?
c: protecting the plant as the outer layer of cells, often with a waxy cuticle
growth at the base of leaves or the internodes
giving support (they are dead cells in the xylem)
items.e: Guard cells: opening and closing the stomata.

items.q: What are the four components of xylem?
c: tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres
sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibres and phloem parenchyma
items.e: Phloem has sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres.

items.q: Which plant tissue is responsible for opening and closing the stomata?
items.e: Guard cells: opening and closing the stomata.

items.q: What is the role of cork in a plant?
c: protecting older stems; its dead cells have suberin, which keeps out water and gases
carrying food from the leaves to other parts of the plant
increasing the girth (thickness) of the stem or root
items.e: Cork: protecting older stems; its dead cells have suberin, which keeps out water and gases.

items.q: What is differentiation?
c: the process by which cells take a permanent shape, size and function
items.e: Meristem cells differentiate into permanent tissues.

items.q: What substance makes cork impervious to gases and water?
items.e: Lignin hardens sclerenchyma.

items.q: Why do meristematic cells lack vacuoles?
c: they divide actively and have dense cytoplasm
items.e: Vacuoles are found in mature cells.

items.q: Which part of phloem is made of dead cells?
items.e: The other parts of phloem are living.

items.q: Which plant tissue is responsible for photosynthesis, as it contains chlorophyll?
items.e: Chlorenchyma: photosynthesis, as it contains chlorophyll.

items.q: Which plant tissue is responsible for increasing the girth (thickness) of the stem or root?
items.e: Lateral meristem (cambium): increasing the girth (thickness) of the stem or root.

items.q: What are the parts of a neuron?
c: a nucleus and a cell wall
a cell body with a nucleus, dendrites and an axon
items.e: A neuron can be up to a metre long.

items.q: What is the role of collenchyma in a plant?
c: carrying food as the tube cells of phloem with perforated walls
protecting the plant as the outer layer of cells, often with a waxy cuticle
living cells next to sieve tubes that help them work
flexibility in leaves and stems, with cells thickened at the corners
items.e: Collenchyma: flexibility in leaves and stems, with cells thickened at the corners.

items.q: Which plant tissue is responsible for carrying water and minerals up from the roots?
items.e: Xylem: carrying water and minerals up from the roots.

items.q: What is the function of red blood cells?
items.e: They have no nucleus in mammals.

items.q: Which plant tissue is made of dead cells?
items.e: The husk of a coconut is sclerenchyma.

items.q: What is the shape of smooth muscle cells?
c: long and spindle-shaped with one nucleus
items.e: They are found in the iris of the eye and the gut.

items.q: What does lignin do in plant cells?
c: it acts like cement and hardens the cell walls
items.e: It is found in sclerenchyma.

items.q: Which tissue stores fat in our body?
items.e: It also works as an insulator.

items.q: What would happen if the ligaments at a joint were damaged?
c: the bones would not stay firmly joined and the joint would be weak
items.e: Ligaments join bone to bone.

items.q: Which plant tissue is responsible for helping aquatic plants float, using large air cavities?
items.e: Aerenchyma: helping aquatic plants float, using large air cavities.

items.q: Which plant tissue is responsible for hardness and strength, with dead cells and lignin in their walls?
items.e: Sclerenchyma: hardness and strength, with dead cells and lignin in their walls.

items.q: What is the role of squamous epithelium?
c: rhythmic contraction of the heart all through life
preventing wear and tear in the skin with several layers of cells
lining the mouth, blood vessels and lung alveoli as a thin, flat layer
helping absorption as tall cells lining the inner wall of the intestine
items.e: Squamous epithelium: lining the mouth, blood vessels and lung alveoli as a thin, flat layer.

items.q: What is the role of cartilage?
c: preventing wear and tear in the skin with several layers of cells
lining kidney tubules and salivary gland ducts with cube-shaped cells
smoothing bone surfaces at joints; found in the nose, ear and trachea
connecting bone to bone, with some elasticity
items.e: Cartilage: smoothing bone surfaces at joints; found in the nose, ear and trachea.

items.q: Which tissue is found in the heel, joining the calf muscle to the heel bone?
items.e: The heel, joining the calf muscle to the heel bone: tendon.

items.q: Which tissue is found in the inner lining of the small intestine?
items.e: The inner lining of the small intestine: columnar epithelium.

items.q: Which animal tissue is described here: lining the mouth, blood vessels and lung alveoli as a thin, flat layer?
items.e: Squamous epithelium: lining the mouth, blood vessels and lung alveoli as a thin, flat layer.

items.q: What is the role of tendon?
c: connecting bone to bone, with some elasticity
pushing mucus forward in the respiratory tract with hair-like cilia
storing fat below the skin and acting as an insulator
connecting muscle to bone, with great strength but little flexibility
items.e: Tendon: connecting muscle to bone, with great strength but little flexibility.

items.q: Which tissue is found in between the skin and muscles?
items.e: Between the skin and muscles: areolar tissue.

items.q: What is the role of ciliated columnar epithelium?
c: smoothing bone surfaces at joints; found in the nose, ear and trachea
helping absorption as tall cells lining the inner wall of the intestine
rhythmic contraction of the heart all through life
pushing mucus forward in the respiratory tract with hair-like cilia
items.e: Ciliated columnar epithelium: pushing mucus forward in the respiratory tract with hair-like cilia.

items.q: What is the role of blood?
c: lining the mouth, blood vessels and lung alveoli as a thin, flat layer
carrying gases, food, hormones and wastes around the body as a fluid
connecting bone to bone, with some elasticity
rhythmic contraction of the heart all through life
items.e: Blood: carrying gases, food, hormones and wastes around the body as a fluid.

items.q: Which tissue is found in the lining of the kidney tubules?
items.e: The lining of the kidney tubules: cuboidal epithelium.

items.q: What is the role of smooth (unstriated) muscle?
c: helping absorption as tall cells lining the inner wall of the intestine
involuntary movements in the stomach, intestine and blood vessels
pushing mucus forward in the respiratory tract with hair-like cilia
carrying gases, food, hormones and wastes around the body as a fluid
items.e: Smooth (unstriated) muscle: involuntary movements in the stomach, intestine and blood vessels.

items.q: What is the role of nerve tissue (neurons)?
c: involuntary movements in the stomach, intestine and blood vessels
connecting bone to bone, with some elasticity
storing fat below the skin and acting as an insulator
items.e: Nerve tissue (neurons): carrying messages as electrical impulses.

items.q: Which animal tissue is described here: forming the hard skeleton, with a matrix of calcium and phosphorus?
items.e: Bone: forming the hard skeleton, with a matrix of calcium and phosphorus.

items.q: What is the role of stratified squamous epithelium?
c: storing fat below the skin and acting as an insulator
preventing wear and tear in the skin with several layers of cells
secreting substances such as sweat and saliva
items.e: Stratified squamous epithelium: preventing wear and tear in the skin with several layers of cells.

items.q: Which tissue is found in the brain and the spinal cord?
items.e: The brain and the spinal cord: nerve tissue (neurons).

items.q: What is the role of glandular epithelium?
c: pushing mucus forward in the respiratory tract with hair-like cilia
storing fat below the skin and acting as an insulator
secreting substances such as sweat and saliva
carrying gases, food, hormones and wastes around the body as a fluid
items.e: Glandular epithelium: secreting substances such as sweat and saliva.

items.q: Which tissue is found in the inner lining of the trachea?
items.e: The inner lining of the trachea: ciliated columnar epithelium.

items.q: Which animal tissue is described here: carrying gases, food, hormones and wastes around the body as a fluid?
items.e: Blood: carrying gases, food, hormones and wastes around the body as a fluid.

items.q: Which animal tissue is described here: helping absorption as tall cells lining the inner wall of the intestine?
items.e: Columnar epithelium: helping absorption as tall cells lining the inner wall of the intestine.

items.q: Which tissue is found in the iris of the eye and the ureters?
items.e: The iris of the eye and the ureters: smooth (unstriated) muscle.

items.q: Which animal tissue is described here: carrying messages as electrical impulses?
items.e: Nerve tissue (neurons): carrying messages as electrical impulses.

items.q: Where are meristems found?
c: at the growing tips of roots and stems, and in the cambium
items.e: Their cells divide actively.

items.q: What is the role of striated (voluntary) muscle?
c: rhythmic contraction of the heart all through life
connecting muscle to bone, with great strength but little flexibility
moving the limbs; its cells are long, unbranched and multinucleate
secreting substances such as sweat and saliva
items.e: Striated (voluntary) muscle: moving the limbs; its cells are long, unbranched and multinucleate.

items.q: What is the role of bone?
c: forming the hard skeleton, with a matrix of calcium and phosphorus
connecting muscle to bone, with great strength but little flexibility
helping absorption as tall cells lining the inner wall of the intestine
filling the space inside organs and supporting them; found between skin and muscles
items.e: Bone: forming the hard skeleton, with a matrix of calcium and phosphorus.

items.q: Which animal tissue is described here: connecting bone to bone, with some elasticity?
items.e: Ligament: connecting bone to bone, with some elasticity.

items.q: What is the role of ligament?
c: connecting bone to bone, with some elasticity
smoothing bone surfaces at joints; found in the nose, ear and trachea
pushing mucus forward in the respiratory tract with hair-like cilia
carrying gases, food, hormones and wastes around the body as a fluid
items.e: Ligament: connecting bone to bone, with some elasticity.

items.q: Which animal tissue is described here: moving the limbs; its cells are long, unbranched and multinucleate?
items.e: Striated (voluntary) muscle: moving the limbs; its cells are long, unbranched and multinucleate.

items.q: Why do plants have more supportive tissue than animals?
c: they are stationary and must stand upright
items.e: Much of this tissue is dead.

items.q: Which tissue lines the inside of the trachea and moves dust out?
items.e: The cilia sweep mucus upwards.

items.q: Which blood cells help in clotting?
items.e: White blood cells fight infection.

items.q: What is the role of columnar epithelium?
c: smoothing bone surfaces at joints; found in the nose, ear and trachea
helping absorption as tall cells lining the inner wall of the intestine
lining the mouth, blood vessels and lung alveoli as a thin, flat layer
preventing wear and tear in the skin with several layers of cells
items.e: Columnar epithelium: helping absorption as tall cells lining the inner wall of the intestine.

items.q: Why is cardiac muscle different from voluntary muscle?
c: it is controlled by our will
it is found in the arms
its cells are multinucleate and unbranched
it contracts rhythmically all through life without tiring and without our control
items.e: Its cells are branched and uninucleate.

items.q: What is a tissue?
c: a group of cells similar in structure that work together to perform a function
items.e: Blood, bone and xylem are tissues.

items.q: What is the role of adipose tissue?
c: storing fat below the skin and acting as an insulator
smoothing bone surfaces at joints; found in the nose, ear and trachea
involuntary movements in the stomach, intestine and blood vessels
preventing wear and tear in the skin with several layers of cells
items.e: Adipose tissue: storing fat below the skin and acting as an insulator.

items.q: What is a nerve?
c: many nerve fibres bound together by connective tissue
items.e: Nerves carry messages around the body.

items.q: Which animal tissue is described here: preventing wear and tear in the skin with several layers of cells?
items.e: Stratified squamous epithelium: preventing wear and tear in the skin with several layers of cells.

items.q: Which animal tissue is described here: lining kidney tubules and salivary gland ducts with cube-shaped cells?
items.e: Cuboidal epithelium: lining kidney tubules and salivary gland ducts with cube-shaped cells.

items.q: What are stomata used for?
c: exchange of gases with the air and transpiration
items.e: Guard cells open and close them.

items.q: What does the waxy cuticle on leaves do?
items.e: Desert plants have a thick cuticle.

items.q: What is the role of cardiac muscle?
c: carrying gases, food, hormones and wastes around the body as a fluid
secreting substances such as sweat and saliva
rhythmic contraction of the heart all through life
connecting bone to bone, with some elasticity
items.e: Cardiac muscle: rhythmic contraction of the heart all through life.

items.q: Which animal tissue is described here: rhythmic contraction of the heart all through life?
items.e: Cardiac muscle: rhythmic contraction of the heart all through life.

items.q: Which plant tissue is mainly found in the growing tip of a shoot?
items.e: The growing tip of a shoot: apical meristem.

items.q: Which tissue is found in the walls of the stomach and intestine?
items.e: The walls of the stomach and intestine: smooth (unstriated) muscle.

items.q: Which plant tissue is mainly found in the outermost layer of a leaf?
items.e: The outermost layer of a leaf: epidermis.

items.q: Which tissue is found in the biceps of the upper arm?
items.e: The biceps of the upper arm: striated (voluntary) muscle.

items.q: Which is the fluid part of blood called?
items.e: Red cells, white cells and platelets float in the plasma.

items.q: Which plant tissue is mainly found in the green tissue of a leaf?
items.e: The green tissue of a leaf: chlorenchyma.

items.q: Which tissue helps aquatic plants float?
items.e: It has big air cavities.

items.q: Which tissue is found in the tip of the nose and the ear?
items.e: The tip of the nose and the ear: cartilage.

items.q: Which tissue is found in the walls of the heart?
items.e: The walls of the heart: cardiac muscle.

items.q: Which tissue is found in the lining of blood vessels and the lung alveoli?
items.e: The lining of blood vessels and the lung alveoli: squamous epithelium.

items.q: Which plant tissue is mainly found in the root tip?
items.e: The root tip: apical meristem.

items.q: Which plant tissue is mainly found in the veins of a leaf carrying water?
items.e: The veins of a leaf carrying water: xylem.

items.q: Which tissue is found in the thigh muscles?
items.e: The thigh muscles: striated (voluntary) muscle.

items.q: Which animal tissue is described here: involuntary movements in the stomach, intestine and blood vessels?
items.e: Smooth (unstriated) muscle: involuntary movements in the stomach, intestine and blood vessels.

items.q: Which tissue is found in the sweat glands of the skin?
items.e: The sweat glands of the skin: glandular epithelium.

items.q: Which animal tissue is described here: connecting muscle to bone, with great strength but little flexibility?
items.e: Tendon: connecting muscle to bone, with great strength but little flexibility.

items.q: Which plant tissue is mainly found in the pith of a stem?
items.e: The pith of a stem: parenchyma.

items.q: Which tissue is found in the skeleton?
items.e: The skeleton: bone.

items.q: Which plant tissue is mainly found in the stalk of a leaf?
items.e: The stalk of a leaf: collenchyma.
